newsitem.title: USA: Nicaragua hopes to sign new IMF pact this year.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua hopes to sign new IMF pact this year.

text.p: Nicaragua hopes to sign a new loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund this year, Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman said on Wednesday.

"The IMF will soon be sending a mission to Nicaragua to discuss a second ESAF (Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility) agreement," he told reporters here after meeting with officials at the White House.

Asked when he expected to clinch a three-year programme, which the IMF grants to countries switching from a centrally planned economy to a market-based system, Aleman replied: "Sometime this year, before December."
Aleman, who is in Washington on a working visit, met earlier on Wednesday with IMF managing director Michel Camdessus.
Nicaragua had signed a first ESAF programme in 1994 under Aleman's predecessor, Violeta Chamorro, as it tried to shore up its economy after a decade-long civil war.
The IMF agreement was suspended late last year because Chamorro's government failed to meet several policy targets including the telephone privatisation and tax reform.
Nicaragua also hopes to benefit eventually from a debt relief programme championed by the IMF and the World Bank, the Highly Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) initiative.

Nicaragua's foreign is about $ 6.0 billion, down from over $11 billion after a series of buybacks and bilateral reductions. The country pays around $300 million a year on its debt, a sum roughly equivalent to half its annual exports.
